G6.2.finding_summary: Audit-AF2 reframe: the recommended-action rule has free oracle access to info["attack_stage"] and is the upper bound on the value of perfect stage detection, not a deployable competing baseline. Best deployable RL agent (A2C, +1336.6) captures 79.3% of the oracle ceiling (+1684.8) without observing attack stages. The reward-misspecification finding persists at deployable scale: A2C mit-rate=0.317 (not the 0.84 seen in the ablation PPO-only probe at n=30). IoTWarden treated as inspiration, not head-to-head baseline.

G6.4.finding_summary: RF-Acting alone exceeds the 3 ms RF budget (~4.6x over) due to sklearn per-call dispatch on a 100-tree ensemble; production deployment would use compiled inference. RL latency claim unaffected: A2C 0.095 ms is 145.8x faster than RF-Acting at a 12% reward cost.

G6.5.title: F8 trained-RL CI does not overlap any non-RL baseline CI
G6.5.notes: All three RL agents are statistically separated from every non-RL deployable baseline (random, always-block, always-observe). Note: RL CIs sit below oracle and RF-Acting — the latency-reward trade-off framing (fast/lower-reward RL vs slow/higher-reward RF) applies.

summary.headline_finding: Best deployable RL agent (A2C +1336.6, 10 seeds, 300 episodes) captures 79.3% of the oracle ceiling (+1684.8) on test_balanced under the primary contract impact_is_terminal=False. Among deployable policies the latency-reward trade-off is: RF-Acting (+1516.0, 13.83 ms p50) vs A2C (+1336.6, 0.095 ms p50) — a 145.8x latency advantage at a 12% reward cost. Benign FPR: DQN 6.1%, PPO 10.2%, A2C 11.5% — FPR is an open limitation elevated to primary threat in the revision.
summary.secondary_finding: compromise_rate=1.0 for all policies — every episode reaches IMPACT; the metric confirms the framework operates as reactive mitigation, not attack prevention. Reward misspecification persists at deployable scale: A2C mit-rate=0.317 at n=300/10-seed benchmark (ablation PPO probe at n=30 reached 0.84 in a controlled setting, not replicated at full benchmark scale).
